target.title: fix(ollama): bound native streaming 200 success-body NDJSON reads at 16 MiB
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two sibling sites in `extensions/ollama/src/` accumulate an unbounded NDJSON byte stream into a string buffer while waiting for `\n` line delimiters. The companion **error-body** path was bounded at 8 KiB by an earlier PR (`OLLAMA_STREAM_ERROR_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES`); the symmetric **200 success-body** paths were left open. A hostile, buggy, or misconfigured Ollama-compatible endpoint (including a self-hosted Ollama with an unusual proxy in front, a corrupt file mirror, or a network-capturing middlebox that streams indefinitely) can cause OpenClaw to grow the string buffer until the gateway OOMs or hits a long-lived RSS ceiling, since `buffer += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true })` is an O(N²) operation in JavaScript.

**Site 1 (chat, /api/chat):** `extensions/ollama/src/stream.ts:1045` (`parseNdjsonStream`) — used by every native Ollama chat / tool-call flow.

**Site 2 (model download, /api/pull):** `extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts:254` — used by `ensureOllamaModelPulled` for pulling Ollama model blobs.

These are the **only two first-party Ollama native NDJSON streaming consumers** in the extension. Capping both in one PR closes the entire Ollama success-body OOM surface.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR bundles two cohesive pieces of work because the helper itself (`src/agents/streaming-byte-guard.ts`, ~87 LoC) is meaningless to extensions without a SDK seam, and the Ollama bound is meaningless without the helper. Together they ship the same bounded-read pattern that #96701, #96723, #96762, #96768, #97535, #97620, #97628, #96920, #96984, #96605 applied to Anthropic streaming, OpenAI Responses streaming, Mistral streaming, runtime proxy, Google OAuth/embedding/TTS/Drive, and other surfaces — but for Ollama native NDJSON.

**Commit 1 (SDK promotion):** Promote `createSseByteGuard` to `openclaw/plugin-sdk/stream-reader-with-limit`. Mirrors the existing `openclaw/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime` pattern (which re-exports `readResponseWithLimit` from `@openclaw/media-core`). The helper itself was already documented as "If extensions need it, promote to a plugin-SDK subpath in a separate, dedicated PR with full SDK metadata sync" — this PR is that promotion, paired with the first planned extension consumer.

**Commit 2 (Ollama chat bound, /api/chat):** Apply `createSseByteGuard` to `parseNdjsonStream` via the caller site in `createOllamaStreamFn`. The 16 MiB cap matches `PROVIDER_TEXT_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024` from `src/agents/provider-http-errors.ts:17` (the canonical streaming cap value already used by all sibling bounded-read PRs). The `parseNdjsonStream` signature is widened from `ReadableStreamDefaultReader<Uint8Array>` to `Pick<ReadableStreamDefaultReader<Uint8Array>, "read">` so it accepts both the wrapped guard and a bare reader — backward compatible with all existing callers and tests.

**Commit 3 (sibling fix, /api/pull):** Apply the same guard to the Ollama model pull path in `setup.ts:254` (`pullOllamaModelCore`). Uses the same 16 MiB cap and identical error shape. The `readOllamaPullChunkWithIdleTimeout` signature is widened to `Pick<ReadableStreamDefaultReader<Uint8Array>, "read" | "cancel">` so it accepts both the bare reader and the guard; the guard's `cancel()` transparently forwards to the underlying reader, so the existing idle-timeout cancel path is unchanged.

**Commit 4 (CI fix):** Update the `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` budget defaults to reflect the new entrypoint — `publicEntrypoints: 323 → 324`, `publicExports: 10412 → 10416`, `publicFunctionExports: 5227 → 5228`. Without this, `checks-node-compact-small-whole-2` fails the 3 budget tests in `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts`.

## User Impact

- Existing successful native Ollama chat / tool-call / model-pull flows keep working — the only new failure modes are `Ollama streaming body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received <size>)` (chat) and `Ollama pull body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received <size>)` (model download) when a streaming endpoint emits >16 MiB before newline-delimited framing. These are the desired safety behaviors.
- Self-hosted Ollama deployments with unusual proxies in front now have a deterministic OOM/DoS ceiling on **both** native NDJSON streaming paths instead of unbounded memory growth.
- 0 user-visible behavior change for normal-sized responses. 0 config / migration / setup impact. 0 new SDK subpath surface beyond the existing `response-limit-runtime` pattern.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (per `real-behavior-proof-structure` 6-field template)

- **Behavior addressed**: unbounded buffering of the Ollama native streaming 200 success-body NDJSON read; after the fix the read is capped at 16 MiB and the underlying reader is cancelled on overflow.
- **Real environment tested**: a real `node:http` server bound to `127.0.0.1` returning a `Content-Length`-less 64 MiB body (4× the cap) chunk-by-chunk with backpressure, plus a small (217 bytes) negative-control NDJSON body, plus a happy-path small NDJSON body. Drives the production `createSseByteGuard` from `src/agents/streaming-byte-guard.ts` over a real TCP socket. Node v22.22.0.
- **Exact steps**: `node --import tsx scripts/_proof_ollama_stream.mts` (proof script kept local-only, not committed, matching Alix-007 #96607 pattern).
- **Evidence after fix** (verbatim terminal output from the local-only proof script, captured 2026-07-03):

  ```
  === Ollama streaming success-body bounded read (cap=16777216, would-stream≈67108864) ===
  cap-trace: bounded reader cancelled at 16750078 bytes (full server body = 67108864); server.bytesSent=19922944
  PASS  Ollama streaming body bounded: rejected with "Ollama streaming body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received 16815604)"; bytesSent=19922944 (< 67108864); overflowed=true; cancelled=true
  --- negative control ---
  PASS  negative control: small body fully drained (217 bytes <= 16777216); cap did not trigger; overflowed=false; cancelled=false
  === All Ollama streaming bounded-read assertions passed ===
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: `createSseByteGuard` cancelled the upstream `ReadableStreamDefaultReader` at ~16 MiB (well under 64 MiB). Server-side `bytesSent` observed at 19-21 MiB across multiple runs — bounded, not drained. `cancel(reason)` received an `Error` instance. The thrown error message uses the canonical `Ollama streaming body exceeded 16777216 bytes (received <size>)` shape (matching #96701, #96723, #96762, #96768 sibling PRs). Negative control confirms the cap is the cause of rejection, not body structure.
- **What was not tested**: live Ollama API call against an actual Ollama installation (the proof exercises the same production helper against the same wire shape the live endpoint would carry); cross-platform Node 18/20 differences (Node 22 only, matches CI).

### Quantitative read-out (Layer 3 inline loopback, per `loopback-proof-required-bounded-read`)

Three runs of the inline `bounds real TCP-streamed NDJSON body without content-length` test, captured via `pnpm test --reporter=verbose` (2026-07-03):

| Run | cap | totalRead (returned) | bytesSent (server) | receivedBytes (error size) | overflowed | cancelled |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 16,777,216 | 16,751,694 | 19,922,944 | 16,817,220 | true | true |
| 2 | 16,777,216 | 16,713,602 | 19,922,944 | 16,779,128 | true | true |
| 3 | 16,777,216 | 16,761,974 | 19,922,944 | 16,827,500 | true | true |

Invariant holds across all runs: `receivedBytes > cap > totalRead`, `bytesSent > totalRead` (server didn't finish before cancel propagated), and both `overflowed` / `cancelled` flags are `true`. The byte counts vary across runs because TCP chunk coalescing varies with kernel timer behavior — the invariant `cap < receivedBytes < bytesSent` is what matters, not exact numbers.

### Inline test coverage (4 tests across 2 test files)

`extensions/ollama/src/stream-runtime.test.ts` (3 tests, 105 total in file):

1. `cancels and throws when bytes exceed 16 MiB` — Layer 2 deterministic overflow via a fake `ReadableStream<Uint8Array>` pull stream with 32 × 1 MiB chunks. Asserts canonical overflow error message (`/^Ollama streaming body exceeded 16777216 bytes \(received \d+\)$/`), `pullCount ∈ [17, 20]` (one in-flight chunk + one TCP-coalesced tail), `cancelReason instanceof Error`, both `overflowed` and `cancelled` flags `true`.
2. `drains small valid NDJSON without overflow` — negative control. Small 2-line NDJSON drains end-to-end with `totalBytes() < 16 MiB` and `overflowed() === false`.
3. `bounds real TCP-streamed NDJSON body without content-length` — Layer 3 real-wire proof. Real `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1:0` streams 64 × 1 MiB chunks with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, no newline terminator. Real `fetch()` against the loopback URL. Real `createSseByteGuard`. Quantitative read-out via `console.log` for PR body evidence.

`extensions/ollama/src/setup.test.ts` (1 new test, 30 total in file):

4. `bounds oversized pull body and cancels the stream` — sibling fix proof. Mirrors the cloud-auth 401 bounded-read test pattern. 64 × 1 MiB chunks streamed to `/api/pull` are bounded at 16 MiB with the canonical `Ollama pull body exceeded N bytes (received M)` error. Asserts `readCount < 64` (stream cancelled well before completion) and the spinner surfaces the canonical error message.

All 135 tests across both files pass: `stream-runtime.test.ts` 105/105, `setup.test.ts` 30/30.

### Out of scope (separate PRs, sequenced)

- `extensions/google/transport-stream.ts:1116` (`parseGoogleSseChunks`) — same bounded-read pattern; blocked on Vincent Koc's #97535 google-bound roadmap (commenting on that PR today).
- `src/llm/providers/anthropic.ts` (`iterateSseMessages`, legacy provider SSE parser) — already covered by #96723.
- `src/agents/runtime/proxy.ts` (`streamProxy`, internal proxy SSE parser) — already covered by #96768.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior change? No — normal-sized responses unaffected; oversized responses on either chat or model-pull paths now throw a clear overflow error instead of silently accumulating memory.
- Config / env / migration change? No.
- Security / auth / secrets / network / tool-execution change? Yes — OOM/DoS protection for both Ollama native streaming success-body paths: chat (`/api/chat`, 16 MiB cap) and model pull (`/api/pull`, 16 MiB cap), each with reader cancellation on overflow.
- Highest-risk area: cancel propagation from `createSseByteGuard` to underlying reader. Verified by explicit test assertion (`expect(cancelReason).toBeInstanceOf(Error)`) in both the inline deterministic test and the loopback test. Sibling fix in setup.ts: the guard's `cancel()` transparently forwards to the underlying reader, so the existing idle-timeout cancel path is unchanged (existing test `fails stalled model pull streams after an idle timeout` continues to pass).
- SDK surface change: 1 new subpath `openclaw/plugin-sdk/stream-reader-with-limit` re-exporting the existing `createSseByteGuard` helper. Mirrors `openclaw/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime` shape. Bundled plugin runtime load cost is unchanged (the helper is only imported on the streaming path, not on plugin startup).
- Self-hosted Ollama compat: the cap fires only when a single chat response or model-pull stream emits >16 MiB before newline framing, which is not reachable from any legitimate Ollama response today (real Ollama chat responses are <1 MiB for typical workloads, <8 MiB for the longest reasoning models; model pull progress events are <100 bytes per chunk). The cap is a safety net, not a behavior change for normal traffic.

## Diff stats

```
10 files changed, 271 insertions(+), 9 deletions(-)
```

- `src/plugin-sdk/stream-reader-with-limit.ts` — new SDK re-export (12 LoC)
- `scripts/lib/plugin-sdk-entrypoints.json` — +1 entry name
- `package.json` — +4 LoC auto-generated by `pnpm plugin-sdk:sync-exports`
- `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` — auto-regenerated by `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:gen --write`
- `docs/plugins/sdk-subpaths.md` — +1 row
- `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` — +3/-3 LoC budget defaults (entrypoints 323→324, exports 10412→10416, callable 5227→5228)
- `extensions/ollama/src/stream.ts` — +9/-1 LoC (1 import + 1 const + wrap block; signature widening is type-only)
- `extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts` — +9/-1 LoC (1 import + 1 const + wrap block + `readOllamaPullChunkWithIdleTimeout` signature widening)
- `extensions/ollama/src/stream-runtime.test.ts` — +177 LoC (3 inline tests + Layer 3 loopback + quantitative read-out)
- `extensions/ollama/src/setup.test.ts` — +53 LoC (1 inline test for /api/pull bounded read)

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs` — typecheck passes (core + extensions)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/ollama/src/stream-runtime.test.ts` — 105/105 tests pass
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/ollama/src/setup.test.ts` — 30/30 tests pass
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` — 8/8 tests pass
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json <4 modified files>` — 0 lint errors
- `node --import tsx scripts/_proof_ollama_stream.mts` — local-only repro script passes
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` — passes
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:check-exports` — passes (regenerated exports match entrypoints list)

## Closes / siblings

- Closes the symmetric success-body gap to `OLLAMA_STREAM_ERROR_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES` (8 KiB error-body bound, existing) on **both** Ollama NDJSON streaming paths: `/api/chat` (chat/tool-call) and `/api/pull` (model download).
- Same 16 MiB cap as #95218, #95420, #96701, #96723, #96762, #96768, #96920, #96984, #97535, #97620, #97628 (all canonical streaming success-body bounded-read PRs).
- First two extension consumers of `openclaw/plugin-sdk/stream-reader-with-limit`. Subsequent extension consumers (Google SSE, future channels) can import from this SDK subpath without touching core.
- Companion SDK promotion commit bundles the helper re-export, entrypoints registration, exports sync, baseline hash regen, and docs row in one cohesive change — no consumer breaks if this PR is reverted, since the SDK seam is gated by the bound consumers in commits 2 and 3.
